name: Ancestry
desc: Runs the Ancestry family-history website and AncestryDNA consumer genetic testing service, with localized sites in several countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1bn in 2022 (company facts, cited on Wikipedia); bought by Blackstone for USD 4.7bn in Dec 2020
markets: US plus country sites for Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Mexico, Sweden and the UK; AncestryDNA sold in 128 countries.
rationale: Consumer subscription brand selling in 128 countries; F1's heritage storytelling and global TV audience suit DNA-test marketing.

name: Simon & Schuster
desc: One of the largest English-language book publishers, with imprints in the US, UK, Australia, India and Canada.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.1bn in 2022; bought by KKR for USD 1.62bn, closed Oct 2023
markets: Worldwide book sales, with operations in the US, UK, Australia, India, Canada and, since 2024, the Netherlands and Belgium.
rationale: Publisher of sports memoirs and F1-adjacent titles; content and licensing tie-ins with teams and drivers could drive book sales.

name: Varsity Brands
industry: cheerleading, school sports apparel and events
desc: Runs cheerleading competitions and camps and supplies school sports uniforms and equipment through BSN Sports in the US.
capacity_detail: Bought by KKR for about USD 4.75bn in August 2024
markets: United States schools, colleges and all-star cheer gyms, with uniforms, equipment, competitions and yearbooks.
rationale: Youth sports brand could use F1's US growth and STEM appeal to reach teenage athletes and schools.

name: Superstruct Entertainment
desc: Owns and runs more than 85 music festivals across Europe and Australia, including Wacken, Sónar and Boardmasters.
capacity_detail: Bought by KKR from Providence Equity Partners for EUR 1.3bn in June 2024
markets: Festivals in the UK, Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Finland, Norway and Australia, plus Boiler Room and Q-dance.
rationale: Live-music festival group could co-promote Grand Prix weekend concerts and fan-zone entertainment across its European markets.

name: DirecTV
desc: US satellite and streaming television provider carrying sports packages from the NFL, NBA, NHL and MLB.
capacity_detail: TPG agreed in Sep 2024 to buy AT&T's remaining 70% stake for USD 7.6bn; closed July 2025, giving TPG 100%
sponsorships: Big Ten Conference sponsorship (2023); Texas Rangers telecasts (2025); NFL Sunday Ticket for business customers
markets: United States, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands; satellite and streaming TV for homes and businesses.
rationale: Sports-led pay-TV brand; F1's growing US audience fits its MySports bundle and bar-and-restaurant business customers.

name: Yahoo
industry: web portal, news and sports media
desc: Runs Yahoo Mail, Yahoo News, Yahoo Finance and Yahoo Sports websites and apps for a worldwide audience.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 7.4bn in 2020; Apollo funds own 90% since Sep 2021
sponsorships: Founding partner of Levi's Stadium (49ers, from 2014); NBA partnership via Yahoo Sports (2018); main sponsor of Pramac Racing MotoGP (2021)
markets: Worldwide audience with localized versions in many countries; left mainland China in 2021.
rationale: Has sponsored MotoGP's Pramac team before; Yahoo Sports and Finance audiences overlap with F1's global fan base.

name: Univar Solutions
desc: Distributes chemicals and food and personal-care ingredients to industrial customers across North America and Europe.
capacity_detail: Revenue about USD 11.5bn in 2022; taken private by Apollo funds at USD 8.1bn enterprise value, closed Aug 2023
markets: Global distributor with operations in the US, Canada, the UK, Ireland, Belgium, the Netherlands and Turkey.
rationale: B2B chemicals distributor; F1 hospitality could serve customer entertainment in North America and Europe, though brand need is low.

name: Arconic
desc: Makes aluminium sheet, plate and extrusions for aerospace, automotive, building and industrial customers.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 8.96bn in 2022; taken private by Apollo in a USD 5.2bn deal, closed Aug 2023
markets: Plants in the United States and Europe, with past operations in the UK, France, China and Russia.
rationale: Aluminium supplier to automotive and aerospace; F1 lightweight-materials engineering story suits a technical-partner deal.

name: Great Canadian Entertainment
desc: Operates casinos, racetracks with slots and gaming centres in Canada, including Great Canadian Casino Resort Toronto.
capacity_detail: Gross gaming revenue about 1.2bn (Canadian dollars) in 2017; taken private by Apollo in Sep 2021
markets: Canada: Ontario, Nova Scotia and other provinces; exiting British Columbia since 2024.
rationale: Casino resort operator in Toronto could use the Canadian Grand Prix for hospitality and player rewards.

name: Atlético de Madrid
desc: La Liga football club playing at the Metropolitano stadium, with a women's team and international academies.
capacity_detail: Apollo Sports Capital controlling stake announced Nov 2025 valuing the club at about EUR 2.2bn; completed March 2026
sponsorships: Kit by Nike since 2001; shirt sponsor Visit Rwanda from 2025, Riyadh Air 2023-24
markets: Spain-based club with a worldwide fan base; revenue EUR 409.5M in 2023-24, 12th in Europe.
rationale: Apollo-backed club seeking global commercial growth; cross-promotion with the Madrid Grand Prix (Madring) from 2026 is a natural fit.

name: Panera Brands
desc: Owns Panera Bread, Caribou Coffee and Einstein Bros. Bagels restaurant chains, mainly in the US and Canada.
capacity_detail: Panera Bread revenue USD 6.456bn in 2023
markets: About 2,178 Panera locations in the US and Canada; Caribou has franchised outlets in several international markets.
rationale: Big US consumer food brand; F1's US races in Miami, Austin and Las Vegas reach its core diners.

name: Chico's FAS
desc: Runs Chico's, White House Black Market and Soma women's clothing and lingerie stores across the US.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.1bn in 2018; bought by Sycamore for about USD 1bn, completed Jan 2024
markets: About 1,376 stores in the US and Canada (2019), plus franchise locations in Mexico and US airports.
rationale: Women's fashion brands could reach F1's fast-growing female US audience through lifestyle and hospitality activations.

name: Talbots
desc: American women's clothing and accessories retailer selling classic styles through about 490 stores and online.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2bn in 2021
markets: United States, with 493 stores (Feb 2021) and online sales.
rationale: Classic US womenswear brand; limited fit, but F1's affluent female US fan growth offers a hospitality-led angle.

name: Etro
desc: Milan luxury fashion house known for paisley prints, selling clothing, accessories and home textiles worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue 372 million in 2018 (USD in infobox, EUR in body text); L Catterton took 60% in 2021
markets: 140 flagship stores in 58 countries including Milan, London, Paris, New York, Beijing, Tokyo and Seoul.

signals.marketing: Founding family completed its exit in Dec 2025 (Dec 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etro)

rationale: Italian luxury house with global boutiques; F1 drivers' apparel and Monaco or Imola hospitality suit a luxury repositioning.

name: Omnissa
industry: digital workspace and device management software
desc: Sells Horizon desktop virtualization and Workspace ONE device management software, formerly VMware's end-user computing division.
capacity_detail: KKR agreed in Feb 2024 to buy Broadcom's end-user computing division for about USD 4bn
markets: Enterprise customers worldwide using former VMware Horizon and Workspace ONE products.
rationale: Former VMware unit that inherited an F1 heritage (VMware partnered McLaren in 2022); a new brand needs global awareness.

name: Nothing Bundt Cakes
desc: Franchised bakery chain selling bundt cakes through shops across the United States and Canada.
capacity_detail: Bought by KKR from Roark Capital for USD 2bn in March 2026
markets: North American franchised bakeries; page read gives no further market detail.
rationale: Fast-growing US treat brand under new owner; F1's US races could support celebration-themed fan marketing, though fit is modest.

name: Arnott's
desc: Australian maker of Tim Tam, Shapes and other biscuits and snacks, with factories across Asia-Pacific.
capacity_detail: Revenue AUD 1.04bn in 2018; bought by KKR from Campbell Soup for USD 2.2bn in 2019
markets: Australia, New Zealand, Malaysia and Indonesia manufacturing; sold across Asia-Pacific and exported worldwide.
rationale: Iconic Australian snack brand; the Melbourne Grand Prix and F1's Asia-Pacific races suit Tim Tam promotions.

name: Viridor
desc: UK recycling and energy-recovery company that turns household and commercial waste into materials and electricity.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 672M in 2023; bought by KKR for GBP 4.2bn in July 2020
markets: United Kingdom councils and businesses; recycling plants and energy-recovery facilities across England, Scotland and Wales.
rationale: F1's net-zero 2030 programme and UK team base create a sustainability partnership angle for waste and recycling.

name: Epicor
industry: ERP software for manufacturers and distributors
desc: Develops enterprise resource planning software for manufacturing, distribution, retail and automotive businesses.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.05bn in fiscal 2022; bought by CD&R from KKR for USD 4.7bn (announced Aug 2020)
markets: Business software customers in the US and internationally; page read does not list countries.
rationale: Manufacturing-software vendor; rivals like SAP, Oracle and IFS use F1 to showcase industrial software credentials.

name: Veritiv
desc: Distributes packaging, facility supplies and printing paper to businesses from 125 centres in the US and Mexico.
capacity_detail: Taken private by CD&R for USD 2.6bn; owned by CD&R since Nov 2023
markets: United States and Mexico, with 125 operating distribution centres; ranked 503rd on the Fortune 500.
rationale: B2B distributor with little consumer branding; F1 hospitality could support customer entertainment, but fit is weak.

name: Opella
desc: Sanofi's former consumer-health arm, making Doliprane, Allegra, Dulcolax, Buscopan and other over-the-counter brands.
capacity_detail: Sanofi agreed in Oct 2024 to sell 50% to CD&R for EUR 10bn; completed April 2025 (CD&R 50%, Sanofi 48.2%, Bpifrance 1.8%)
markets: Sold worldwide, with main sites in Europe, North and Latin America, the Middle East, Asia and Australia.
rationale: Newly independent consumer-health group building its own brand; global F1 reach suits OTC brands like Allegra and Doliprane.

name: The Weather Company
desc: Runs the Weather Channel app, weather.com and Weather Underground, and sells weather data to advertisers and aviation.
capacity_detail: Bought from IBM by Francisco Partners for USD 1.1bn (incl. deferred and contingent payments); closed Feb 2024
markets: Consumer weather apps and websites used worldwide, plus B2B data for advertising and aviation customers.
rationale: Weather drives F1 race strategy; a forecasting-partner deal gives the brand on-screen data credits like rivals in timing and analytics.

name: Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma
desc: Japanese pharmaceutical company developing and selling prescription medicines in Japan, the US and other markets.
capacity_detail: Bain Capital agreed in Feb 2025 to acquire it from Mitsubishi Chemical for JPY 510bn (USD 3.4bn)
markets: Japan, the United States (Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma America) and Israel (NeuroDerm).
rationale: Newly independent drugmaker needing corporate profile; Japanese Grand Prix offers domestic visibility, though pharma promotion is restricted.

name: Chelsea F.C.
desc: Premier League football club based at Stamford Bridge, London, with men's and women's teams.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 592M in 2025 (Forbes, cited on Wikipedia); Clearlake took full control of owner BlueCo in Sep 2026
sponsorships: Kit by Nike since 2017; front-of-shirt partner Circle Internet Group for 2026-27
markets: Premier League and European competitions with a worldwide fan base and global commercial partners.

signals.marketing: Clearlake took full control and Todd Boehly stepped down as chairman (Sep 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C.)

rationale: Global football brand under new single owner; cross-sport content and hospitality tie-ins with an F1 team build its US fan base.

name: Intrado
desc: Provides 911 emergency-call infrastructure and enterprise communications and collaboration services, formerly named West Corporation.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.6bn in 2012; bought by Apollo for USD 5.2bn in Oct 2017
markets: Mainly US public-safety and enterprise customers; page read gives no country list.
rationale: Communications-infrastructure provider; F1's real-time connectivity story offers a technical showcase, though consumer fit is low.

name: Intertape Polymer Group
desc: Makes packaging tapes, stretch and shrink films and protective packaging for industrial and e-commerce customers.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.5bn in 2022; taken private by Clearlake in June 2022
markets: Sites in the US, Canada, India, China, Germany, Portugal and the UK; most sales in North America.
rationale: Industrial packaging maker; F1 logistics and team-supplier status could support B2B marketing, but brand need is limited.

name: Insight Global
desc: Staffing company placing IT, engineering, finance and healthcare professionals with US and UK employers.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 4.5bn (Forbes, cited on Wikipedia; year not stated); Leonard Green led the 2016 buyout
markets: United States, plus a UK subsidiary (Global Insights Ltd).
rationale: Staffing rivals Randstad and ManpowerGroup already sponsor F1; a deal would help it compete for talent and clients.

name: AdvancedMD
desc: Cloud software for independent US medical practices covering scheduling, billing and electronic health records.
capacity_detail: Bought from Global Payments by Francisco Partners for USD 1.125bn; agreed Oct 2024, completed Dec 2024
markets: Independent medical practices in the United States.
rationale: US-only healthcare software; F1 fit is weak beyond US hospitality for clinic-group customers.

name: Precisely
industry: data integrity and location data software
desc: Sells data integration, data quality, location intelligence and data enrichment software to large enterprises.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 600M in 2020; re-acquired by Clearlake with TA Associates for a reported USD 3.5bn in March 2021
markets: Enterprise customers worldwide; page read does not list countries.
rationale: Data-software vendor; F1's data-driven racing lets rivals like Snowflake and Oracle showcase analytics, a model Precisely could follow.

name: Sabre Hospitality Solutions
desc: Provides the SynXis hotel reservation, distribution and property software used by hotel chains and independent hotels.
capacity_detail: Sabre's hospitality solutions business bought by TPG for USD 1.1bn in 2025 (completed July 2025)
markets: Hotel customers worldwide; pages read give no country list.
rationale: Hotel-tech business newly separated from Sabre; F1 race weekends drive hotel demand, giving a B2B hospitality showcase.

name: OSTTRA
desc: Post-trade processing and data network for over-the-counter derivatives and FX markets, formerly an S&P Global-CME venture.
capacity_detail: Bought by KKR from S&P Global and CME Group for USD 3.1bn in April 2025
markets: Banks and asset managers in global OTC derivatives and FX markets; page read gives no country list.
rationale: Newly independent fintech infrastructure brand; F1 hospitality is a proven way to entertain bank and trading clients.

name: GoTo (LogMeIn)
desc: Sells LogMeIn remote-access and IT-support software and GoTo Connect business phone and meeting tools.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.262bn in 2019; bought by Francisco Partners and Evergreen Coast Capital (Elliott) for USD 4.3bn, closed Aug 2020
markets: Businesses and IT teams worldwide; page read gives no country list.
rationale: Rivals TeamViewer and Cisco Webex sponsor F1 teams; GoTo could match them to promote remote IT support.

name: Rona
desc: Canadian home improvement and building-supply retailer operating about 425 stores under Rona, Rona+ and other banners.
capacity_detail: Revenue CAD 4.2bn in 2013; Lowe's Canadian operations sold to Sycamore, closed Feb 2023
sponsorships: Sponsored TV series Rona Dream Home (2004) and My Rona Home (2009)
markets: Canada, with about 425 stores across Rona, Rona+, Rona Cashway, Moffatt & Powell and Dick's Lumber banners.
rationale: Large Canadian retailer; the Montreal Grand Prix in its home province offers strong local visibility and trade hospitality.

name: Auctane
desc: Formerly Stamps.com, provides online postage and shipping software such as ShipStation for e-commerce sellers.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 757.98M in 2020 (as Stamps.com); taken private by Thoma Bravo, closed Oct 2021
markets: E-commerce merchants mainly in the US, plus international shipping software users; page read gives no country list.
rationale: Shipping-software brand for online sellers; F1 logistics storytelling could support small-business marketing, though fit is modest.

name: Acumatica
desc: Cloud enterprise resource planning software for small and mid-sized businesses, sold through partners in several countries.
capacity_detail: Acquired by Vista Equity Partners from EQT for USD 2bn in 2025
markets: United States, UK and Ireland, Australia and New Zealand (via MYOB partnership).
rationale: Mid-market ERP challenger; rivals SAP, Oracle and IFS use F1 to signal scale, a play for brand awareness.

name: Mills Fleet Farm
desc: Upper Midwest retailer of farm supplies, hunting, fishing, automotive and home goods through about 50 stores.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 712.3M in 2022; sold to KKR in 2016
markets: Upper Midwest United States, with 50-53 stores in Wisconsin, Minnesota and neighbouring states.
rationale: Regional rural retailer; NASCAR is a better fit than F1, so relevance is low.

name: KIKO Milano
desc: Italian make-up and skincare brand selling through more than 1,100 own stores in 66 countries and online.
capacity_detail: Net revenue about EUR 800M in 2023; L Catterton agreed to buy a majority stake from the Percassi family in April 2024
markets: More than 1,100 stores in 66 countries, mainly Europe and the Middle East, with planned US expansion.
rationale: Italian beauty brand planning US entry; F1's young female fan growth and Italian races suit a cosmetics partnership like ELEMIS.

name: Safe Harbor Marinas
desc: Largest US marina and superyacht servicing business, running 138 marinas in the United States and Puerto Rico.
capacity_detail: Bought by Blackstone Infrastructure funds from Sun Communities for USD 5.65bn; completed May 2025
markets: 138 marinas across the United States and Puerto Rico, offering boat storage, servicing and superyacht berths.
rationale: Superyacht clientele overlaps F1's wealthy audience; Miami Grand Prix hospitality and marina tie-ins fit naturally.

name: Tropical Smoothie Cafe
desc: Franchised fast-casual chain selling smoothies, wraps, sandwiches and bowls through more than 1,750 US cafes.
capacity_detail: Blackstone agreed in April 2024 to buy it from Levine Leichtman for nearly USD 2bn (source close to deal); completed June 2024
markets: United States, with 1,750+ franchised cafes (2026) across most states.
rationale: Fast-growing US health-food chain; F1's young US audience at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas suits its brand-building.

name: York Holdings
desc: Japanese retail group owning Ito-Yokado and York-Benimaru supermarkets, Loft, Akachan Honpo and Denny's Japan.
capacity_detail: Seven & i sold York Holdings' supermarket and specialty-store businesses to Bain Capital for JPY 814.7bn (about USD 5.5bn); completed 1 Sep 2025
markets: Japan supermarkets and specialty stores; Ito-Yokado also has stores in Beijing and Sichuan, China.
rationale: Large Japanese consumer retailer under new ownership; the Suzuka Japanese Grand Prix could support a domestic rebranding push.
